analysis:
This PR changes documentation only: docs/provider/troubleshooting.md and docs/reference/configuration.md. No code is visible, so all behavior below is as described in the docs and is unverified.

Security-relevant changes:
1. New `DARKBLOOM_VERIFIED_WEIGHTS_FILE` (configuration.md head line 371). It adds a persisted weight-hash verification cache that skips re-hashing at startup registration. The record is bound to stat metadata and is described only as owner-only. Combined with the 'publishes its own per-file SHA-256 verification instead of bracketing passes' wording (head ~584-590), this relates to T-012 and T-027 (operator weight substitution, A-004). Reported as a low finding. I could not verify the record's integrity protection, the store's implementation, or whether the coordinator treats the weight hash as self-reported.
2. The page-cache drop after hashing (`PageCache.drop`) and the `DARKBLOOM_MEMORY_AVAILABILITY` description change are availability and memory-admission details. I saw no confidentiality impact. `free-only` still fails closed.
3. The troubleshooting additions are the `glm wired limit` doctor check and the sysctl/LaunchDaemon remediation. It runs `sudo sysctl -w` with fixed numeric values, and the provider never invokes sudo itself. The root LaunchDaemon plist is created manually by an administrator at a fixed system path, not from user-writable paths. No fan-helper or TB-010 style escalation is introduced.

Remaining questions for deeper review: the VerifiedWeightHashStore implementation (file permissions, symlink handling, MAC or authentication, behavior on stat mismatch), and whether the managed GLM load still detects mid-load weight modification.

findings.detail: The new `DARKBLOOM_VERIFIED_WEIGHTS_FILE` (`~/.darkbloom/verified-weights.json`) lets startup registration reuse a recorded weight hash instead of re-hashing when the stored device/inode/size/mtime/ctime match. The documented protection is only 'owner-only'. The owner is the provider operator (ADV-001), so the operator can hand-write a record for substituted weights, or edit the weights and restore their stat metadata under a manipulated clock or inode reuse. The provider would then register and advertise the previously verified hash without re-reading the bytes. This narrows the existing weight-substitution control (T-012/T-027) and adds a new operator-writable trust input. The same docs say a managed GLM load now publishes its own per-file SHA-256 verification 'instead of bracketing passes', which drops the pre/post-load comparison. The threat model should record that this cache is self-attested local state, not an integrity proof, and that coordinator-side hash checks must not treat it as stronger evidence. If the cache is intended as a security control, it should be MAC-bound to the Secure Enclave-rooted KEK or limited to non-security fast paths.
findings.title: Weight-hash verification cache keyed on stat metadata with no stated integrity protection
